title: Replying to @Emma #theatre #arts #nyc #top5
transcript: Here are my top 5 favorite theatre venues in New York. I did a video with some of the most beautiful venues, but as this person pointed out, beauty isn't everything. Sometimes the most beautiful venues are also the least comfortable. My actual favorite venues are intimate, flexible, good sight lines, spacious lobbies, sufficient bathrooms, and if you're really lucky, maybe even comfortable seats. In fifth place I have MCC. I know a lot of people don't like the cold concrete aesthetic, but I don't mind it. The main space can house some pretty large productions, while the auditorium itself feels very intimate, which I think is kind of a magic combo. That does mean it's a little too wide though, Depending on the staging, some of the side seats are not great. I do think it's pretty comfortable though. The smaller black box space is also solid, and the lobby is pretty spacious. In fourth place I have the Bushwick Starr. It's essentially a really nice black box. It looks completely different every time you're in there. The lobby is also pretty spacious, although I do wish there was more seating. I believe there are five single person bathrooms, which is surprisingly a lot for a theatre of this size. And they put the communal sink area outside of the bathrooms themselves, which makes everything run pretty quickly. In third place I have St. Ann’s Warehouse. Also a very cool, versatile space. Again, the lobby and bathrooms are very spacious and they have kind of a modern aesthetic without feeling cold or unwelcoming. Also, you step outside and see one of the most beautiful views of the New York City skyline. There's also this beautiful garden with the archways. I've seen people do their wedding photo shoots here and I don't even know if they realized it was part of a theatre. On the downside, while they can configure the space in a million different ways, they do have a standard end on configuration that they do for a lot of their productions. And I think when you're sitting in the back rows, it can feel very far away. And I would say the leg room tends to not be great. Second place, I have the Signature Center. In general, all three of their spaces are great, but I think the Griffin is my favorite. Similar to MCC, even with a mezzanine, it feels extremely intimate. There's not a bad seat in the house. And of course, the signature has by far the best theatre lobby in New York City. It honestly feels more like a communal third space than a theatre lobby. It's open during the day, you can go in there, use the bathrooms. But I think my number one favorite is the Claire Tow Theatre at Lincoln Center. It's all the things I've been praising this whole time: Intimate, comfortable. But the main reason it's number one is that buying a ticket to a show here, which are all, by the way, only about $35 Also grants you access to this gorgeous rooftop terrace with an absolutely stunning view of Lincoln Center and the city beyond.
classificationReason: Reply-to-comment video ('Replying to @Emma') listing the creator's top 5 favorite theatre venues in New York. Not about any specific production.
